html:
A prince of the Yamato court in Japan who served as regent for his aunt, Empress Suiko, from 593 until his death in 622. Later Japanese saw him as the founder of their civilisation, and much of his legend grew after his death.

Japan in his day was the Yamato state, a loose league of clans. Working with the powerful Soga clan, he pushed it toward a Chinese model of government and toward Buddhism, which had arrived from Korea a few decades before.

  • He is credited with the Seventeen-article constitution of 604, a moral code for officials.
  • He set up a system of twelve court ranks, shown by the colour of a cap.
  • He sent embassies to Sui China, treating its emperor as an equal, which annoyed the Chinese court.
  • He founded temples, among them Hōryū-ji near Nara.

Historians now doubt how much of this was his own work. Still, the direction he stood for led on to the Taika Reform of 645 and the Chinese-style state of the 700s.
